scope.evidence: All new files serve entities/members/settings: six actions, three Livewire components and views, policies, models/enum, factories, two migrations, routes, both lang files, and docs/CHANGELOG. No out-of-scope onboarding, switcher, middleware, locale or navbar work; the only extra behaviour is the self-removal session/redirect block (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:57-61).

issues.explanation: The test is named 'owner and admin remove members' but both calls act as the owner, so removing another member as an admin through the component (and that path's interaction with the last-manager rule) is never exercised; the policy test only covers the ability in isolation.

The test title says memberships are deleted 'with the entity or the user', but only the user-deletion branch runs; the entity branch is covered indirectly by the settings delete test, so the name overstates the test.

$targetMembershipId is a client-writable public property without #[Validate]/rules(); the action resolves and rejects invalid values with 403 as the task requires, but this is an explicit exception to the Livewire rule that every public input property be validated.

Each member row calls can('assignRole') and can('delete'), and each policy check runs its own membershipFor() query, so rendering the list adds roughly two membership queries per row; resolving the actor's membership once would be leaner.

Self-removal unconditionally forgets current_entity_id and redirects home even when the removed entity is not the session's current entity; clearing it only when it matches would avoid dropping an unrelated selection.

review.summary: The change implements the entities/entity_memberships schema (including the generated owner_seq column and unique-owner index), the Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole models and factories, the policies, the pick endpoint, and the three authorized Livewire entity pages, with lang and documentation updates and a broad Pest suite. It meets the task and the project conventions; the main gap is a test that claims to cover admin removal but only exercises the owner, plus a few nits around the unvalidated transfer-target property, per-row authorization queries, and the unconditional session clear on self-removal. I would approve it once those small items are addressed.
